The main takeaway from our work is that

, in addition to increasing the power to identify associated alleles, high-density genotyping can be targeted to individuals who are likely to be informative and who are most cost-effective to genotype.

genomewide association analyses can be greatly facilitated by genotyping only a small number of individuals at high density and using the resulting genotype information to infer genotypes for the remainder of the pedigree, with little or no loss in power.

the cost and experimental burden of high-density genotyping can be substantially reduced by genotyping a subset of individuals from each pedigree, while still achieving the same level of statistical power.
